Northwest Arkansas ADHD testing: evaluation scope and cost questions

Which ADHD evaluations are available in Northwest Arkansas?

Fayetteville and nearby Springdale offer several different paths to an ADHD assessment. Midtown Counseling describes an ADHD testing battery with a clinical interview, rating scales, attention-task performance and review for other mental-health concerns. The Center for Psychology and Counseling advertises diagnostic testing for ADHD across children, teens and adults. The University of Arkansas Psychological Clinic describes affordable psychological evaluations, but its current site does not publish an ADHD-specific cash price. These offerings should not be treated as identical comprehensive neuropsychological examinations.

What do local ADHD assessments cost?

The local primary sources reviewed here do not establish directly comparable all-in prices for these particular ADHD assessments. Midtown says insurance coverage varies by plan; U of A describes low-cost psychological assessment without stating an ADHD-specific price. UAMS Northwest notes that confirmatory evaluations may leave patients with out-of-pocket costs and advises requesting an estimate when scheduling. Ask for a written quote covering intake, tests, scoring, feedback, report, and any extra visits. A therapy-session price is not a full diagnostic-assessment price.

Confirm the service and clinician before booking

UAMS Northwest Student Wellness explicitly says it offers ADHD-related medical and behavioral care but does not provide confirmatory ADHD diagnostic assessments. Likewise, the University of Arkansas Pat Walker psychiatry team says it does not provide diagnostic ADHD testing. This is crucial when a patient needs evaluation documentation for treatment or accommodations. Verify the specific clinician's Arkansas license, age groups served, test scope and report format. A directory listing is a research lead, not a verified appointment or endorsement.

Screening versus focused diagnostic testing versus comprehensive evaluation

An online questionnaire or brief attention screening can inform a discussion, but is not always sufficient for a diagnostic question, medication documentation or education accommodation. Midtown's described battery combines multiple assessment methods, while a comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation may investigate broader memory, learning, executive-function and cognitive concerns. UAMS recommends an extended face-to-face assessment and follow-up for its confirmatory-documentation needs. Ask the actual receiving school, clinician or accommodation office exactly what report will be accepted.

Six questions before an appointment

Ask whether the practice evaluates adults, children or both. Ask which clinical interview and standardized assessment components are included. Ask whether the assessment looks for anxiety, depression, sleep problems or learning disorders that may resemble ADHD symptoms. Confirm whether you receive a signed written diagnostic report and a feedback visit. Ask about the total cash price, insurance eligibility and waiting list. Finally, verify whether the report meets the needs of the prescriber, employer or academic office requesting it.

Where to begin in Fayetteville, Springdale and Rogers

Start with the University of Arkansas Psychological Clinic, Midtown Counseling, or the Center for Psychology and Counseling to clarify scope and eligibility; contact directly rather than assuming openings. UAMS Northwest maintains a broader local resource list, including other specialists and practices. For adults, note that Northwest Arkansas Psychiatry says its ADHD testing is for under-18 patients and that adults seeking ADHD treatment must provide outside testing. No provider listed here is a verified advertiser or contracted lead recipient, and this page does not rank clinical quality.
